headline: MLOps Engineer Salary in the US in 2026
metaDescription: MLOps engineer salary in the US in 2026: average base pay $130K-$165K, entry level from $90K, senior averages near $209K, and top total pay above $300K.

sections.content:
MLOps engineers in the United States earn a national average base salary of roughly $130,000 to $165,000 in 2026, depending on the source. Salary.com puts the average near $131,000, while Glassdoor reports an average base of about $161,411, with a typical range of $132,000 to $199,000.

The full range is unusually wide, running from about $90,000 at entry level to more than $300,000 in total compensation for senior engineers at top companies once equity and bonuses are included. The spread reflects the fact that one job title covers several different sub-roles.
sections.title: What MLOps engineers earn in 2026

sections.content:
Entry-level MLOps engineers with zero to two years of experience typically earn $90,000 to $132,000 in base pay. Mid-level engineers with three to five years earn roughly $130,000 to $175,000, with total compensation of $145,000 to $200,000.

Senior engineers with five to eight years average around $206,000 to $209,000 in base pay, and staff or principal engineers with eight or more years reach $210,000 to $257,000 in base salary. At FAANG companies and leading AI labs, senior total compensation regularly passes $300,000 once equity is counted.
sections.title: Pay by experience level

sections.content:
MLOps is not one uniform job. Salary guides describe three sub-roles sharing the title: ML platform engineers who build internal machine learning tooling, ML infrastructure engineers who focus on Kubernetes and cloud compute, and applied MLOps engineers who handle model deployment and monitoring.

Pay varies with the sub-role and the employer. An LLMOps or ML-platform specialization can command a premium of 30 to 50 percent over a generalist MLOps band, according to 2026 industry guides. Specialized skills such as Kubeflow, Vertex AI, or SageMaker add a further premium of roughly 8 to 12 percent.
sections.title: Why the title covers three different jobs

sections.content:
Location moves the number sharply. San Francisco-based MLOps engineers earn an average base of about $218,000, roughly 35 percent above the national figure, and New York and Seattle also pay meaningfully above the median. Remote roles at top-tier companies can match those figures, but the highest bands still cluster in the major tech hubs.

The fastest route to higher pay is deep Kubernetes and Terraform experience combined with production model deployment, plus LLM serving skills, which carry a reported premium of $20,000 to $30,000. Note that this is rarely a first job: entry-level openings make up only about 3 percent of postings, so most engineers transition in from software engineering, DevOps, or data engineering.
